summary.text: Rick Beard of Omaha is the Legal Marijuana NOW nominee for governor, a wine professional and private chef. He is running on a state-run medical cannabis program that he says could raise new revenue for property-tax relief, along with an industrial hemp industry and limits on corporate and political action committee money.

paragraphs.text: Beard is a wine professional and private chef and a former farmer; one listing also describes him as a winemaker.
Beard won the Legal Marijuana NOW primary on May 12, 2026, with 69.1% of the vote over James Charvat, and chose Omaha Housing Authority commissioner Keenya Barnes as his running mate.

In a July 2026 interview with the Nebraska Examiner he listed his priorities as medical cannabis and industrial hemp programs, getting corporate and political action committee money out of state politics, and a pause on data center development with mandated closed-loop cooling systems.

He said a state-run medical cannabis program, in which the state would hire farmers, buy facilities and oversee land, could generate $100 million in new tax revenue a year, rising to as much as $500 million.

sources.title: Beard talks priorities, pivot from Nebraska primary election to Nov. 3 faceoff
